name: Kappa and Meen Curry
subtitle: mashed tapioca with a fierce red fish curry, the pairing Kerala argues about

ingredients.note: cassava is what is meant; yam is the closest thing in this pantry
kudampuli, the smoked fish tamarind, is authentic; kokum is the nearest available

prepNotes: Two separate pots. The tapioca is boiled and mashed with coconut; the fish curry is cooked in a clay pot and stays thin and sharp.
The curry should be aggressively sour and salty. It is a sauce for a bland, starchy partner.

steps.text: Boil the tapioca in salted water until a knife slides through, about 25 minutes. Drain well.
Crush the coconut with half the shallots, the green chilli and turmeric, and mash it through the hot tapioca.
For the curry, soak the kokum in 200ml warm water.
Fry the remaining shallots, fenugreek and curry leaves in the coconut oil, add the chilli powder and fry 1 minute.
Add the kokum with its water, bring to a boil, then slide in the fish and simmer 10 minutes without stirring.
steps.tip: Do not stir. Shake the pan instead or the fish breaks up.

steps.text: Rest 15 minutes before serving alongside the mashed tapioca.

storage: The curry keeps 2 days refrigerated and improves overnight. The tapioca is best fresh; it stiffens hard when cold and needs steaming to revive.
